title: Use Aggregate Devices to Rename USB Audio Devices
summary: A workaround to fake-rename USB audio devices in MacOS
content:
I bought a new monitor last week to play GTA VI, among other things, and for boring reasons I won't get into here, I had occasion to plug in two USB audio dinguses — one for my headphones and one for my speakers. The problem with that even though I have two entirely different devices, they are both called "USB Audio Device" in MacOS and as far as I can tell, there's no way to directly rename them. Currently my list looks like this:

$ SwitchAudioSource -a -t output
DELL S2725QC
USB Audio Device
USB Audio Device
MacBook Pro Speakers

What you can do is create an aggregate device in the Audio MIDI Setup app so when you look at your list of outputs either in Settings or in a CLI tool like switchaudio-osx, it will have a useful name.

Open Audio MIDI Setup, hit the plus button, choose Create Aggregate Device, give it name, then tick the audio device you want to "rename". I did this for my speakers and my headphones so now when I run SwitchAudioSource I see two USB Audio Device listed but also my new Speakers and Headphones outputs. There's no way to remove the generic-named devices but this is much better solution that accidentally choosing the wrong output when I want to switch.

$ SwitchAudioSource -a -t output
DELL S2725QC
USB Audio Device
USB Audio Device
MacBook Pro Speakers
Speakers
Headphones
